cards.title: Client brief: ChaiCart
cards.subtitle: What the Sharks want
cards.body: Launch in 6 weeks in 5 Indian cities Customer data must stay in India Team knows Python & JavaScript Tight budget, startup credits welcome Wants AI recommendations 20× traffic spikes on cricket match days

cards.title: You are AWS
cards.subtitle: Launched 2006 — the pioneer
cards.body: Largest market share & broadest service catalogue Biggest partner & startup ecosystem Indian regions: Mumbai, Hyderabad Amazon Bedrock for GenAI They will ask: “Isn't AWS complicated and pricing confusing?”

cards.title: You are Microsoft Azure
cards.subtitle: Enterprise & hybrid champion
cards.body: Works with Microsoft 365, Teams, Entra ID, GitHub Strong hybrid (Azure Arc) story Indian regions: Central India (Pune), South India (Chennai), West India (Mumbai) + more Azure OpenAI / AI Foundry They will ask: “Aren't you only for big corporates?”

cards.title: You are Google Cloud
cards.subtitle: Data & AI native
cards.body: BigQuery analytics, Vertex AI, Gemini models, TPUs Kubernetes was born at Google (GKE) Indian regions: Mumbai, Delhi Huge global private network They will ask: “Your enterprise footprint is smaller — will you be around?”

cards.title: You are Oracle Cloud (OCI)
cards.subtitle: The database powerhouse
cards.body: Oracle Database & Autonomous Database Strong price-performance claims Indian regions: Mumbai, Hyderabad Oracle Database available inside Azure/AWS/Google They will ask: “Why would a chai startup need Oracle?”

cards.title: TWIST: Diwali Mega Sale
cards.body: 50× traffic for 6 hours. No extra budget. What scales? What gets cached? What goes into a queue?

cards.title: TWIST: Region outage
cards.body: Your primary cloud region is down for 2 hours. What keeps working?

cards.title: TWIST: New data law
cards.body: All customer personal data must stay in India, and users can request deletion.

cards.title: TWIST: CFO says cut 30%
cards.body: Reduce the monthly bill by 30% without hurting checkout.

cards.title: Order service
cards.subtitle: Station 1
cards.body: Take a blank ticket. Write an Order ID (e.g. CC-001) and the customer name. Write your timestamp. Pass to Payment.

cards.title: Payment service
cards.subtitle: Station 2
cards.body: Write PAID and the amount. Write your timestamp. Pass to Kitchen. If the facilitator taps you — freeze!

cards.title: Kitchen service
cards.subtitle: Station 3
cards.body: Draw a chai cup on the ticket. Write your timestamp. Pass to Delivery.

cards.title: Delivery service
cards.subtitle: Station 4
cards.body: Write a rider name. Write your timestamp. Pass to Notification.

cards.title: Notification service
cards.subtitle: Station 5
cards.body: Write “SMS sent”. Write your timestamp. Drop it in the DONE pile.

cards.title: The monolith
cards.subtitle: Round 1 only
cards.body: You are the whole restaurant. Do ALL five steps yourself on each ticket, one ticket at a time.

cards.title: Commerce / order app
cards.subtitle: Shopify, custom app
cards.body: Say: “Order CC-1042 placed, ₹180, paid by UPI.” Stamp and pass to CRM.

cards.title: CRM
cards.subtitle: Salesforce, Dynamics 365, Zoho
cards.body: Say: “Priya gets 18 loyalty points. 5th order this week — VIP!” Stamp and pass to ERP.

cards.title: ERP – Finance
cards.subtitle: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle, Dynamics 365
cards.body: Say: “Invoice generated, GST recorded, revenue booked.” Stamp and pass to SCM.

cards.title: SCM – Inventory
cards.subtitle: SAP IBP, Oracle SCM
cards.body: Say: “Milk stock at Koramangala below 10 L — purchase order raised to dairy supplier.” Stamp and pass to HCM.

cards.title: HCM – People
cards.subtitle: Workday, SuccessFactors, Darwinbox
cards.body: Say: “Rider Ravi completed delivery — ₹25 incentive added to payroll.” Stamp and pass to BI.

cards.title: BI – Analytics
cards.subtitle: Power BI, Tableau, Looker
cards.body: Say: “Ginger chai sales up 30% at 4 PM in Bengaluru!” Stamp. Done!

cards.title: ITSM
cards.subtitle: ServiceNow, Jira Service Mgmt
cards.body: Only act if something breaks! Say: “Incident INC-771 opened, on-call engineer paged, customer notified.”

cards.title: Order token #CC-1042
cards.body: 2 Masala Chai + 1 Samosa · ₹180 · Koramangala ☐ Commerce ☐ CRM ☐ ERP ☐ SCM ☐ HCM ☐ BI

cards.title: The Cloud Architect
cards.subtitle: “I see the whole city before it is built.”
cards.body: You: design systems — pick services, draw diagrams, balance cost vs reliability vs security. Skills: networking, identity, databases, Well-Architected thinking, communication. Certs: AZ-104 → AZ-305 · AWS SA Associate/Professional. A day: design reviews, whiteboards, customer calls.

cards.title: The DevOps Engineer
cards.subtitle: “Nothing ships by hand while I am around.”
cards.body: You: build CI/CD pipelines and automate everything from code to production. Skills: Git, Linux, scripting, Docker, pipelines, IaC. Certs: AZ-400 · Terraform Associate · CKAD. A day: fixing a flaky pipeline, speeding up builds, helping devs ship.

cards.title: The Site Reliability Engineer
cards.subtitle: “I guard the nines.”
cards.body: You: keep production reliable using software engineering — SLOs, automation, incident response. Skills: coding, Linux, Kubernetes, observability, calm under pressure. Certs: CKA · cloud associate level · observability certs. A day: reviewing SLOs, killing toil, leading a postmortem.

cards.title: The Platform Engineer
cards.subtitle: “I build the roads others drive on.”
cards.body: You: build the internal developer platform — self-service environments, templates, golden paths. Skills: Kubernetes, IaC, APIs, developer empathy. Certs: CKA/CKS · Terraform Associate. A day: a new “create service” template in the developer portal.

cards.title: The Cloud Security Engineer
cards.subtitle: “Trust nothing. Verify everything.”
cards.body: You: secure identities, networks and data; hunt misconfigurations; respond to threats. Skills: IAM, networking, encryption, policy-as-code, threat modelling. Certs: SC-900 → AZ-500 · AWS Security Specialty · CKS. A day: fixing a public storage finding before attackers do.

cards.title: The FinOps Analyst
cards.subtitle: “Every rupee in the cloud has a name.”
cards.body: You: make cloud spend visible and efficient — tagging, forecasting, savings plans, showback. Skills: cloud pricing, Excel/Power BI, SQL, negotiation. Certs: FinOps Certified Practitioner · AZ-900. A day: “Why did the bill jump 40%?” — and finding out.

cards.title: The Observability Engineer
cards.subtitle: “I see what others cannot.”
cards.body: You: make systems observable — instrumentation, dashboards, alerting, SLOs, AIOps. Skills: OpenTelemetry, metrics/logs/traces, query languages (DQL, KQL, PromQL), APM tools. Certs: Dynatrace Associate · cloud monitoring certs. A day: turning a 2-hour outage into a 2-minute alert.

cards.title: The AI / MLOps Engineer
cards.subtitle: “I teach machines, then keep them honest.”
cards.body: You: take AI models to production — pipelines, GPUs, evaluation, monitoring, cost control. Skills: Python, ML basics, containers, cloud AI services, data engineering. Certs: AI-900 → AI-102 · Azure Data Scientist · Vertex AI / Bedrock learning paths. A day: deploying a chatbot and checking it doesn't hallucinate prices.

posters.name: Netflix
posters.tag: From a DVD outage to chaos engineering
posters.challenge: In 2008 a major database corruption stopped Netflix from shipping DVDs for about three days. One big data centre meant one big point of failure.
posters.did: Netflix moved to AWS public cloud over several years, completing the migration in early 2016. It rebuilt its monolith as many microservices and invented Chaos Monkey, a tool that randomly shuts down production servers so engineers are forced to build systems that survive failure.
posters.q: Would you let a “monkey” randomly kill ChaiCart servers? What would you need first?

posters.name: Disney+ Hotstar
posters.tag: Crores of fans, one final over
posters.challenge: Live cricket brings enormous spikes. Traffic can jump within seconds when a star batter walks in, or crash when a wicket falls. Streams set records, with around 5.9 crore concurrent viewers reported during the 2023 World Cup final.
posters.did: The engineering team talked publicly about pre-scaling infrastructure ahead of big moments because reactive autoscaling can be too slow. They also run massive load tests and game days, use CDNs heavily, and plan “panic mode” features that switch off non-essential services to protect the video stream.
posters.q: What would ChaiCart switch off first to survive an IPL-final spike?

posters.name: UPI / NPCI
posters.challenge: India wanted instant, interoperable, near-free digital payments between any bank and any app, available 24×7.
posters.did: NPCI launched UPI in 2016 as an API-based platform connecting banks and apps like PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm. It now handles 10+ billion transactions a month. Being critical financial infrastructure under RBI rules, it runs in NPCI-controlled data centres with high redundancy, a private-cloud-style model.
posters.q: Why might UPI choose a private/regulated setup when Netflix chose public cloud?

posters.name: IRCTC Tatkal
posters.challenge: Tatkal booking opens at a fixed time. Huge numbers of users (and bots!) hit the site at exactly the same second for a limited number of seats.
posters.did: Railway ticketing has invested over the years in more capacity, caching, CAPTCHA and bot protection, queueing and rate limiting, and a better mobile app. The problem is unusual because demand is predictable in time but far larger than supply.
posters.q: If ChaiCart gave away 100 free chais at 4:00 PM, how would you stop the app from melting?

posters.name: Capital One
posters.tag: A bank goes all-in on public cloud
posters.challenge: A large US bank wanted to move faster, use data and AI, and stop running its own data centres.
posters.did: Capital One went all-in on AWS and announced in 2020 that it had closed its last data centres. It also lived through the downside: a 2019 data breach linked to a misconfigured web application firewall, a hard lesson in the shared-responsibility model.
posters.q: Who was responsible for the breach: the bank or the cloud provider? Why?

posters.name: Spotify
posters.tag: From own data centres to Google Cloud
posters.challenge: Spotify ran its own data centres. Engineers spent time managing hardware instead of building features for millions of listeners.
posters.did: Spotify announced its move to Google Cloud in 2016, attracted by managed data and analytics services. Its engineers also built Backstage, an internal developer portal that was open-sourced and became a CNCF project. It kicked off the platform engineering trend.

questions.label: Top offender: Open Services . Which service has the highest failure rate in the last 2 hours? What's the rate?
Slowest service: Which service has the worst response time ? Is it median or p95/p99 that looks bad?
Follow the ticket: Open Distributed Traces and pick a failed request. How many spans does it have? Which span took longest?
Who calls whom? From a service, look at its incoming and outgoing calls (service flow / Smartscape). Name 2 services it depends on.
Problem solver: Open Problems . Pick one problem. What's the root cause entity, and how many entities were affected?
Error detective: In Logs or a Notebook , run this. When was the error peak? fetch logs | filter loglevel == "ERROR" | makeTimeseries errors = count(), interval: 5m
questions.query:
fetch logs
| filter loglevel == "ERROR"
| makeTimeseries errors = count(), interval: 5m

questions.label: Saturation check: Is any host above 80% CPU? timeseries cpu = avg(dt.host.cpu.usage), by: { dt.entity.host }
Bonus: Write your own DQL query that lists the top 5 slowest services by p95 . Hint: fetch spans , summarize , percentile(duration, 95) , sort , limit .
Inspect the deployed ChaiCart App Service in Central India. What is its public URL?
Place demo orders. If Application Insights ingestion is configured, what is the peak requests/sec? Otherwise use the evidence supplied by the facilitator.
Metric explorer: In Monitor → Metrics , chart “Requests” and “Response time” for the web app. What's the average response time?
Request /chai-not-found. Record the status code and where the failed request appears in the configured observability tool.
If Application Insights is configured, run the supplied KQL and explain the results. Otherwise explain the prepared evidence.
questions.query:
requests
| summarize count() by resultCode, bin(timestamp, 1m)
| order by timestamp desc
